content: 1. In 2013, a study published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease explored the prevalence and management of latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI). 2. Hovell MF, Sipan CL, Blumberg EJ, Hofstetter CR, Slymen D, Friedman L, et al., conducted a controlled trial in 2003 to increase adherence to LTBI treatment among Latino adolescents. The findings were published in the American Journal of Public Health. 3. Kominski GF, Varon SF, Morisky DE, Malotte CK, Ebin VJ, Coly A, et al., analyzed the costs and cost-effectiveness of adolescent compliance with LTBI treatment in a randomized trial, with results published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 2007. 4. Nyamathi A, Christiani A, Nahid P, Gregerson P, and Leake B conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing two treatment programs for homeless adults with LTBI. The study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2006. 5. Goldberg S, Wallace J, Jackson J, Chaulk C, and Nolan C examined the role of cultural case management in LTBI treatment. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2004. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidance in 2010 on the ethical considerations for tuberculosis prevention, care, and control. 7. Denholm JT, McBryde ES, and Brown GV evaluated the ethical implications of immigration screening policies for LTBI. Their work was published in the Australian and New Zealand Journal of Public Health in 2012. 8. Kass NE proposed an ethics framework for public health, which was published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2001. 9. The Republic of Korea, Kuwait, and Latvia were identified as high-income countries with varying TB incidence rates in 2013, as part of the primary target countries for LTBI management guidelines. 10. Spain and Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) were also included in the analysis, with Spain having a low TB incidence rate and Venezuela classified as an upper-middle-income country with a moderate TB incidence rate. 11. Systematic reviews were conducted to address key questions related to LTBI management, including: The prevalence of LTBI among risk groups. Predictive investigations and clinical parameters for ruling out active TB in at-risk individuals. Tests or combinations of tests that best identify individuals at high risk of progressing to active TB. The most effective treatment options for LTBI, based on systematic literature reviews and meta-analyses. Monitoring and managing hepatic toxicity and other adverse events during LTBI treatment. The potential development of drug resistance due to LTBI treatment. The effectiveness of anti-tuberculosis drugs in preventing active TB in contacts of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) patients. Initiation and completion rates for recommended LTBI treatment regimens. Determinants of treatment initiation, adherence, and completion for LTBI regimens. Interventions with proven efficacy to improve LTBI treatment initiation, adherence, and completion. Whether the duration of protection from LTBI treatment poses a barrier to implementation. The cost-effectiveness of LTBI management interventions.
